summary: ER visit and laparoscopic appendectomy billed at full chargemaster rates with no insurance on file. This is a nonprofit hospital, so financial assistance under IRS 501(r) is the biggest lever — and at $36,000 for a household of two you are inside the range most hospitals write off entirely.

do_first.action: Call Patient Financial Services at (813) 555-0190 and ask for the Financial Assistance application, an itemized bill with codes, and a hold on the account.
do_first.why: You're inside the 120-day window before this can go to collections. Nothing else moves until the application is in.

deadlines.what: Account may be referred to collections
deadlines.consequence: Leverage drops and the hospital may no longer apply charity care directly.

errors_found.how_to_dispute: Ask billing to remove the duplicate and issue a corrected statement.

errors_found.issue: Operating room billed 4 × 30 min — confirm actual OR time on the operative report
errors_found.how_to_dispute: Request the operative report and compare documented OR time to quantity billed.

errors_found.issue: Pharmacy $3,120 is a single unitemized line
errors_found.how_to_dispute: Request per-drug itemization with NDC codes.

levers.name: Charity care — IRS 501(r) financial assistance
levers.applies_because: Nonprofit hospital. $36,000 for 2 people ≈ 170% of the Federal Poverty Level; most 501(r) policies write off 100% up to 200% FPL.
steps: Call Patient Financial Services and request the Financial Assistance Policy application.
Ask for a hold on the account while it's reviewed.
Submit with 2 recent pay stubs, last tax return, 2 bank statements, proof of household size.
Get the decision in writing. If denied, appeal — denials are often reversed.
levers.script: Hi, I'm calling about account ending 4471, date of service September 17. I'd like to apply for your Financial Assistance Program under your 501(r) policy. Please send me the application, place a hold on this account while it's reviewed, and send a fully itemized bill with CPT codes. I'm not agreeing to a payment plan until the application is decided.

levers.name: Itemized bill audit and error dispute
levers.applies_because: Three visible issues already: a duplicate supplies line, an OR quantity that doesn't match a typical appendectomy, and an unitemized pharmacy charge.
steps: Request an itemized statement with CPT/HCPCS and NDC codes.
Compare every line to what happened.
Dispute duplicates and unsupported items in writing; keep copies.
levers.script: Please send a fully itemized statement with CPT/HCPCS and NDC codes for date of service 09/17/2026. I'm disputing the duplicate 'Surgical supplies' charge on lines 7 and 11 and requesting documentation for the operating-room time billed. Please issue a corrected statement.

levers.name: Prompt-pay discount on any remaining balance
levers.applies_because: Whatever survives financial assistance can usually be reduced 20–40% for a lump-sum payment.
steps: After the assistance decision, ask for the self-pay / prompt-pay rate on the remainder.
levers.script: What is your prompt-pay or self-pay discount if I settle the remaining balance in full this month?

teach.q: Why does it matter that the hospital is a nonprofit?
teach.a: Nonprofit hospitals don't pay most taxes. In exchange, federal law — IRS section 501(r) — requires them to have a written financial assistance policy and to tell patients about it. Most don't advertise it, but they can't refuse to give you the application.

teach.q: How do I know if I qualify?
teach.a: Almost always it's your household income compared to the Federal Poverty Level. For two people the 2026 FPL is about $21,150. Many hospitals write off 100% up to double that, and a sliding scale up to three or four times.

teach.q: Why ask for an itemized bill before paying anything?
teach.a: A summary bill hides the line items. Roughly 80% of hospital bills contain at least one error, and you can only dispute what you can see.

Most hospitals send unpaid accounts to a collection agency around 120 days after service. Once that happens, the hospital's own programs are harder to apply, and your leverage drops. Act inside the window.
